source_text: CELIA. By all means, do—as a sport. But don't love any man in earnest, and don't go further even in sport than you can safely retreat from with an honorable blush.
modern_text: CELIA. Marry, I prithee, do, to make sport withal; but love no man in good earnest, nor no further in sport neither than with safety of a pure blush thou mayst in honour come off again.

source_text: Freeze, freeze, you bitter sky, That do not bite so near As benefits forgot; Though you warp the waters, Your sting is not so sharp As a friend remembered not. Heigh-ho! sing, &c.
modern_text: Freeze, freeze, thou bitter sky, That dost not bite so nigh As benefits forgot; Though thou the waters warp, Thy sting is not so sharp As friend rememb'red not. Heigh-ho! sing, &c.

source_text: ROSALIND. By my troth, and in good earnest, and so God mend me, and by all pretty oaths that are not dangerous, if you break one jot of your promise, or come one minute behind your hour, I will think you the most pathetical break-promise, and the most hollow lover, and the most unworthy of her you call Rosalind, that may be chosen out of the gross band of the unfaithful. Therefore beware my censure, and keep your promise.
modern_text: ROSALIND. By my faith, and in good earnest, and so God mend me, and by all pretty oaths that are not dangerous, if you break one jot of your promise, or come one minute behind your hour, I will think you the most pathetical break-promise, and the most hollow lover, and the most unworthy of her you call Rosalind, who may be picked out of the gross band of the unfaithful. So beware my censure, and keep your promise.
